style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontFamily=Georgia;fontSize=22;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=4;" value="<b><u>NOTES:</u></b><div><b><font style="font-size: 20px;">• API Gateway Decision</font></b></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;"><span class="hover:entity-accent entity-underline inline cursor-pointer align-baseline" style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • <u>Amazon API Gateway</u></span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"> is best for serverless architectures</span></font></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • latency Overhead</font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Higher Cost when scaled up</font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Poor at internal service routing (service level routing) for Kubernetes&nbsp;</font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • A <u>Custom Gateway </u>like Fastify Gateway is a good choice to start with, but not great for long-term</font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Low Maintainability<br><b>&nbsp; &nbsp; • Kong is the winner here, with Horizontal Pods for scaling</b></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><i>&nbsp; &nbsp; • May move to Istio/Envoy in the future as it scales up</i></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font style=""><span style="font-size: 20px;"><i>&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; Client → CloudFront → ALB → Istio/Envoy Gateway → NATS/Kafka services</i></span></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font style=""><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b><br></b></span></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font style=""><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• Kong: fast to implement, good for mostly external APIs and simple multi-tenant routing</b></span></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;"><font style=""><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• Envoy/Istio: Long-term scalability, full microservice observability, mTLS, global assurance</b></span></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><br></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• <u>NATS with KAFKA Decision</u></b></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><i>NATS: Clustered</i></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><i>KAFKA: Multi-Broker Cluster</i></font></span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><font style="font-size: 20px;"><b>&nbsp; <u>WHY NATS: for service messaging</u></b></font></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>&nbsp; &nbsp; • NATS </b>excels at service-to-service communication using Request-Reply, great for RPC, KAFKA is not ideal here</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; •&nbsp;</span><i style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 20px;">Very&nbsp;</i><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 20px;">High Throughput and&nbsp;</span><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Ultra Low Latency (microseconds ~0.5-2ms) as it avoids HTTP Layers</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Simple Protocol, easier to implement, low learning curve</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Ephemeral message delivery, lower-level persistence, NATS wins here, Service Bus like CQRS, Real-Time messaging, <i>KAFKA is an overkill</i></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Extremely Lightweight, small memory footprint, fast clustering, <i>KAFKA is heavy for edge environments</i></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; line-height: 160%;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • NATS Cluster: 3 Nodes, minimal tuning, fast startup, good for cold starts<br></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>&nbsp; <u>WHY KAFKA: event streaming</u></b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • KAFKA is for durable event storage, large-scale data pipelines, and analytics</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Event Sourcing is necessary for multi-tenant SaaS</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Reply events, rebuild state, event-driven architecture, stream processing, data warehousing (in scale), large retention policy</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Ultra High Throughput(&gt;1M events/sec)</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; •&nbsp;</span><font style="font-size: 20px;"><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Multi-tenant event sourcing:&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Partition by </span><code class="bg-text-200/5 border border-0.5 border-border-300 text-danger-000 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded-[0.4rem] px-1 py-px text-[0.9rem]" style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">tenant_id</code><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"> for isolation and ordered replay</span></font></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">---</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">API → NATS (service comm) → Microservices</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">Events → KAFKA (event store) → Analytics / Pipelines</span></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">---</font></div><div><br></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;"><b><u>• EMAIL Service Decision</u></b>: SES in comparison with Sendgrid</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • SES is the most cost-effective</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Full Control, can scale to millions of emails</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Best For Transactional Emails, while SendGrid is good for marketing emails</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • &lt;100k emails/month -&gt; SendGrid is good</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • &gt;100k emails/month -&gt; SES</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;"><br></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 21px;"><b style="">• Database Decision</b></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• Primary Transaction DB: PostgreSQL</b></font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Multi-AZ architecture, PgBouncer for Connection Pooling</font></div><div><font style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Primary (writes) → Streaming Replication → Read Replicas</font></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Used for: `tenants, users, workflow_definitions, workflow_instances, workflow_transitions, payments`</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • ACID, Strong Consistency, Optimistic Locking, Row Level Security</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• Audit Event Store</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • MongoDB</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • append-only log, flexible schema, fast event retrieval</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; • User For: audit_logs, state_change_events, workflow_execution_history</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;"><br></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;"><b>• Cache Layer:&nbsp;</b></span><b style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Redis via Elasticache</b></div><div><b style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><br></b></div><div><b style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">• Multi-Tenant Isolation</b></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Tenant ID Propagated everywhere: JWT → API Gateway → Services</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Used for RLS, Kafka Partitioning, rate limiting</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Large tenants may be isolated to a dedicated workflow execution cluster</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><br></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>• High Availability: Multi-AZ Deployment</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • All services deployed across Multiple AZs</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Load Balancer in place</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Database Replicas and backups are regularly made</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b><br></b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>• Fault Tolerance</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Circuit breakers on external APIs, Webhooks, and the notification service</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • KAFKA DLQ in place with AWS SQS</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; • Retry with Exponential backoff</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><br></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>• Disaster Recovery</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>&nbsp; &nbsp; • PostgreSQL</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; • WAL archiving → AWS S3</span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; • Daily Snapshots</span><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px;">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; • point-in-time recovery, snapshotting</span><span style="font-size: 20px;"></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"><b>&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;• MongoDB</b></span></div><div><span style="font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), KAFKA Communication
1. All service to Audit Log
2. Service to Analytics
3. Service to Notifications, DLQ
4. Chat Service, for history

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 754px; height: 1px; padding-top: 47px; margin-left: 4297px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Georgia; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.font: • Poor at internal service routing (service level routing) for Kubernetes
• A Custom Gateway like Fastify Gateway is a good choice to start with, but not great for long-term

• Low Maintainability
• Kong is the winner here, with Horizontal Pods for scaling

font.i: • May move to Istio/Envoy in the future as it scales up

span.i: Client → CloudFront → ALB → Istio/Envoy Gateway → NATS/Kafka services

span.b: • Kong: fast to implement, good for mostly external APIs and simple multi-tenant routing
• Envoy/Istio: Long-term scalability, full microservice observability, mTLS, global assurance

div.span: • NATS excels at service-to-service communication using Request-Reply, great for RPC, KAFKA is not ideal here

i.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 20px;

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); font-size: 20px;
font-size: 20px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.span: Ultra Low Latency (microseconds ~0.5-2ms) as it avoids HTTP Layers
• Simple Protocol, easier to implement, low learning curve
• Ephemeral message delivery, lower-level persistence, NATS wins here, Service Bus like CQRS, Real-Time messaging, KAFKA is an overkill
• Extremely Lightweight, small memory footprint, fast clustering, KAFKA is heavy for edge environments
• NATS Cluster: 3 Nodes, minimal tuning, fast startup, good for cold starts
• KAFKA is for durable event storage, large-scale data pipelines, and analytics
• Event Sourcing is necessary for multi-tenant SaaS
• Reply events, rebuild state, event-driven architecture, stream processing, data warehousing (in scale), large retention policy

code.class: bg-text-200/5 border border-0.5 border-border-300 text-danger-000 whitespace-pre-wrap rounded-[0.4rem] px-1 py-px text-[0.9rem]

div.font: • EMAIL Service Decision: SES in comparison with Sendgrid
• Full Control, can scale to millions of emails
• Best For Transactional Emails, while SendGrid is good for marketing emails
• Multi-AZ architecture, PgBouncer for Connection Pooling

div.span: • Used for: `tenants, users, workflow_definitions, workflow_instances, workflow_transitions, payments`
• ACID, Strong Consistency, Optimistic Locking, Row Level Security
• append-only log, flexible schema, fast event retrieval
